material_units.source_text: Vector and derivative notation occurs in later applications. You can follow the scalar examples first; Primer A and Primer B include first-course refreshers before using those tools.
material_units.proposed_reason: Curricular route explains later vector/derivative notation and permits scalar-first reading; it names primer refresher content without asserting a mathematical result.

material_units.source_text: Start with the Easy exercises in one section. Try each question before opening its hint, and write your reasoning before checking the answer. After checking, close the answer and try the question again from memory.
material_units.proposed_reason: Specific study instructions for attempt, hint, reasoning and recall; no theorem, numerical output or proof conclusion is asserted.

material_units.source_text: If a calculation is slowing you down, rebuild it one operation at a time. The examples below are enough to start the set and function exercises; you do not need calculus for Sections 1–3.
material_units.proposed_reason: Pedagogical advice to rebuild calculations and start the elementary sets/functions route before calculus; no quantitative mathematical guarantee.

material_units.source_text: Start by listing elements and reading symbols aloud. The Medium exercises ask you to translate statements; the Hard exercises combine quantifiers with constraints. If a definition feels unfamiliar, revisit this section before trying again.
material_units.proposed_reason: Study instructions and difficulty descriptions for the local set/quantifier practice; no quantified mathematical assertion about sets or controls.

material_units.source_text: Decide whether each statement is true. Explain a true universal statement, give a witness for a true existential statement, and explain why a false statement fails.
material_units.proposed_reason: Task instruction asks the learner to decide and justify the following statements; it does not itself assert those statements.

material_units.source_text: Negate both statements, keeping the domains unchanged. Then decide whether the original statements are true.
material_units.proposed_reason: Task instruction asks for negation and truth assessment with fixed domains; actual negated formulae occur in separately pending mathematical descendants.

material_units.source_text: Negate statement (1) and assess its negation.
material_units.proposed_reason: Instruction to assess the negation of the earlier numbered statement; it supplies no logical identity or truth claim.

material_units.source_text: The Easy exercises refresh function notation and substitution. Medium adds preimages and contraction estimates; Hard asks you to explain which assumptions make an argument work. If a definition feels unfamiliar, revisit this section before trying again.
material_units.proposed_reason: Local practice route/difficulty descriptions and revisit instruction; merely names notation, preimages and assumptions without proving them.

material_units.source_text: A proof is a chain of statements, each following from assumptions, definitions or earlier steps by a rule you can name.
material_units.proposed_reason: Pedagogical account of how to write a proof as justified steps; no theorem, application safety guarantee or particular chain of mathematical implications is supplied.

material_units.source_text: Write a reason beside each step. Easy exercises practise one proof move; Medium builds complete arguments; Hard combines the proof with an audit of its assumptions. If a definition feels unfamiliar, revisit this section before trying again.
material_units.proposed_reason: Advice to annotate proof steps and revisit unfamiliar definitions; describes exercise difficulty goals without asserting their mathematical outputs.

material_units.source_text: For gradual practice on the opening material, use the graded sets on sets & logic, functions & fixed points, and proofs. The exercises below bring together ideas from across the primer.
material_units.proposed_reason: Direct study-navigation instruction to graded sets/functions/proofs practice and the mixed review below; no theorem or computational assertion.

material_units.source_text: You are ready for Primer A when you can read and negate a quantified statement, compose two functions, and explain the difference between a bound and an attained optimum. Check these without opening a solution:
material_units.proposed_reason: Pedagogical readiness checklist asks learners to try subsequent recall tasks; no necessary-and-sufficient mathematical prerequisite theorem.

material_units.source_text: Explain why the grid margin is needed, then turn the explicit error bound into a budget.
material_units.proposed_reason: Instruction to explain a grid margin and convert an error bound to a budget; no actual grid inequality or numeric budget is asserted.

material_units.source_text: If one task stalls, revisit its review link and attempt the local Easy exercise again. You can continue once Easy and Medium work is independent; the Hard exercises are useful return visits as later modules give the ideas context. Next: Primer A: vectors and matrix tools.
material_units.proposed_reason: Study-route advice and next-primer navigation; learner independence is an instructional recommendation, not a mathematical claim.
